claim: An independent RDKit-2026.03.2 + closed-form-distribution audit lifts the module's two pure-oligomer property receipts (EEW series, hydroxyl value) from SINGLE oligomers to POLYDISPERSE mixtures, which is what a real resin is, and then attacks the result. (1) PARITY: the four structural constants and three OHV values already signed by dgeba-oligomer-eew-series-v1 and dgeba-oligomer-hydroxyl-value-v1 are re-derived independently and match to <=5e-4 (7/7 rows). (2) THEOREM (polydispersity invariance): because every ideal linear DGEBA oligomer contributes EXACTLY 2 epoxide equivalents and EXACTLY n hydroxyl equivalents while mass is additive, both titrations are ratios of number-averages of quantities LINEAR in n, so both depend on the distribution ONLY through its first moment <n> - there is no Jensen gap and no dispersity term. Verified numerically on Flory-1936 most-probable, Poisson, and adversarial bimodal (n=0 with n=8/12/40) mixtures at three commercial advancement levels: across a dispersity span of up to 6.77x at matched <n>, the mixture EEW spread is EXACTLY 0.000 g/eq and every deviation from the single-oligomer formula and from the shipped n_bar inversion is <1e-9. The shipped EEW-band -> n_bar inversion is therefore a genuine mixture property, not an artifact of assuming a pure oligomer - a strictly stronger result than the two prior receipts supported. (3) IDENTITY: eliminating <n> between the two titrations yields a zero-parameter cross-titration identity between two INDEPENDENT ASTM methods, OHV = A*(1 - E0/EEW) with A = 56100/M_repeat = 197.2874 mg KOH/g and E0 = M0/2 = 170.2095 g/eq - both already fixed by the prior receipts, nothing fitted - closing on the pure-oligomer series to <1e-12 mg KOH/g over n=0..20. (4) H0 REFUTED: the hypothesis that this identity is robust to realistic DGEBA end-group defects (<=1% relative residual up to 5 mol% alpha-glycol / chlorohydrin ends, both epoxide-consuming) fails - 12 of 16 defect rows at >=1 mol% breach the 1% bar, worst case 41.02% relative, and the residual is strictly monotone in defect load while zero-defect rows sit on the identity to <1e-9 (perfect specificity). The same defects bias the shipped n_bar inversion upward by up to 30.2% relative. (5) The breach is NOT uniform, and that is the second finding: relative detector power falls 17.25x from the liquid grade (<n>=0.13, ideal OHV 19.33 mg KOH/g, 8/8 rows breach, 9.79% residual per mol% glycol) to the semisolid grade (<n>=2.35, ideal OHV 130.70, only 4/8 breach, 0.57% per mol%), because the defect hydroxyl rides on an ever larger ideal-backbone hydroxyl baseline. A single fixed relative acceptance bar is therefore NOT a valid QC rule across the DGEBA grade range. (6) Specificity 4/4: an ideal Flory resin is correctly NOT flagged while 20 mol% phenyl glycidyl ether diluent (+15.67%), 10 mol% free bisphenol-A (+60.68%) and 5 mol% fully hydrolyzed DGEBA diol (+70.54%) are all correctly flagged. The smallest refuting residual exceeds IUPAC-2021 atomic-weight uncertainty on the identity constant by 15.1x, so the signal is chemical, not numerical.

G2_polydispersity_invariance.claim: EEW and OHV of an ideal linear DGEBA mixture depend on the distribution ONLY through its first moment <n>; both are exactly dispersity-invariant, so the shipped EEW -> n_bar inversion is a genuine mixture property.

G3_H0_end_group_defect_robustness.H0: The EEW<->OHV cross-titration identity (and hence the EEW -> n_bar inversion) is robust to realistic DGEBA end-group defects: <=1% relative residual for up to 5 mol% alpha-glycol and/or chlorohydrin ends.
G3_H0_end_group_defect_robustness.interpretation: Two distinct results. (i) The invariance proved in G2 is an IDEAL-SERIES property only: it survives arbitrary polydispersity but NOT epoxide-consuming end groups, which add hydroxyl and remove epoxide simultaneously and so move EEW and OHV off the one-parameter curve in different directions. The residual is therefore not noise - it is a zero-parameter DETECTOR of non-ideal DGEBA, monotone in defect load. (ii) The detector's power is strongly GRADE-DEPENDENT. On low-advancement liquid grades every defect row breaches the bar, because the ideal hydroxyl baseline is small and the two extra OH per hydrolyzed end are a large relative perturbation. On advanced grades the backbone already carries a large ideal OHV, the same defect is a small relative perturbation, and only the heavier loads breach. Relative sensitivity therefore falls by ~17.2x from the liquid to the semisolid grade, so a single fixed relative acceptance bar is NOT a valid QC rule across the DGEBA grade range.
G3_H0_end_group_defect_robustness.refutation_basis: Universal claim refuted by counterexample: 12 of 16 defect rows at >=1 mol% total defect breach the 1% relative bar, worst case 0.4102 relative. The breach is NOT uniform, and the non-uniformity is the second finding.

G4_detector_sensitivity_and_specificity.detection_floor_note: The assumed relative titration precisions are PARAMETRIC sensitivity inputs chosen by this audit, NOT quoted ASTM D1652/D4274 precision statements; no repeatability figure is claimed from the standards.

maps_to_module_hypothesis: Tests the mixture-level validity of the module's shipped EEW-band -> n_bar advancement inversion. Establishes that the inversion is exactly dispersity-invariant (a strictly stronger result than the pure-oligomer receipts supported), and REFUTES the implicit robustness assumption behind it by showing that epoxide-consuming end groups bias it while simultaneously breaking the EEW<->OHV identity - which converts the identity into a zero-parameter QC detector whose power is quantified here, and shown to be grade-dependent rather than uniform.
